Article Title: 'No double standards on terrorism': PM Modi's message at SCO summit in presence of Pak PM Shehbaz Sharif
Article Text:
PM Modi called for dismantling the entire ecosystem that enables terrorism at SCO

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said there can be no “double standards” in the fight against terrorism and called for dismantling its entire ecosystem, including financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens.Addressing the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, PM Modi described terrorism as a “grave challenge to all of humanity” and said the fight against it cannot be limited to a mindset of “action-reaction”.“We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism--its financing, recruitment, radicalization, and safe havens. We must speak in one voice that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,” he said.“Those countries that use terrorism as an instrument of their policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism cannot be a ‘strategic asset’ for anyone,” the Prime Minister added.He also outlined "Security, Connectivity and Opportunity" as the three pillars of India’s vision for the SCO, with peace and security forming the first pillar.“Our shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan,” he said, adding that India would continue its development and humanitarian assistance to the Afghan people.On the West Asia crisis, Modi said conflicts in one region can have repercussions across the world, affecting “energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains of the entire world”.“The countries of the Global South have to bear the maximum brunt of this. Therefore, India's call has been that the solution to all tensions and wars is not possible on the battlefield, but only through Dialogue and Diplomacy,” he said.The Prime Minister also flagged drug trafficking as a serious threat to the younger generation and regional security, calling for stronger cooperation through SCO mechanisms dealing with security threats, organised crime, information security and narcotics. “We must make them effective mediums for practical coordination and timely action,” PM Modi said.He further stressed that SCO cooperation should translate into tangible benefits for people, with people-to-people ties placed at the centre of the grouping’s future agenda.“The true measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts have created for young people, how many new markets have opened up for our entrepreneurs, how much our farmers have benefited from technology, and how much better the lives of our citizens have become,” he said.Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov is hosting the summit and serving as its chairman. PM Modi is attending alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other leaders of SCO member states.
Article Summary: PM Modi called for dismantling the entire ecosystem that enables terrorism at SCO Summit. He outlined "Security, Connectivity and Opportunity" as the three pillars of India’s vision for the SCO. He also flagged drug trafficking as a serious threat to the younger generation and regional security.

Article Title: 'Chhatron ki Goonj' reaches Indore as Rahul eyes BJP's vulnerabilities with "best city" as example
Article Text:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. (Photo: ANI)

NEW DELHI: Amid continuing reverberations from Rahul Gandhi ’s girl-students rally in Pune, the Congress youth outreach “Chhatron ki Goonj” is set to move to another BJP stronghold, the education hub of Madhya Pradesh.Sources said the next episode of “chhatron ki goonj” will be held in Indore on Sep 12.In what is a carefully crafted strategy to challenge the ruling party with the “angry demographic” that led the Jantar Mantar protest, Congress has picked the venue owing to the fact that there has been a history of paper leaks in the state including the infamous examination scandal “Vyapam scam”. Besides, the opposition has won two by-elections “against the might of the state”, the latest being Datia assembly last month.Sources said the party considered a few cities, including in the Congress-ruled states in the south, but then decided on Indore in a bid to continue pressuring the BJP.While the city is a students’ hub and also has a fair share of urban and middle-class population, it has been in the negative spotlight for repeated infrastructural crises – the most sensational being 24 deaths from consuming sewage contaminated water in February 2026.A smart city road, said to be constructed at the cost of Rs 40 crore, collapsed recently, hogging the headlines. Also, there have been allegations of corruption targeting the CM.The “chhatron ki goonj” started in Kota in Rajasthan (June) and then moved to Dehradun (July) and then Prayagraj (August), focusing on examination and employment issues. But in Pune last month, Rahul changed tack when he made it an exclusive event for girls, and his interactive speech around gender justice and “manusmriti” received favourable feedback besides triggering the opponent BJP.The “CKG” strategists are chuffed by the reaction and said the programme will move across the nation with the objective of becoming a “brand” that the youth will associate with.After Indore, the party may choose a city in any of the Congress-ruled states in the south to cover a key region with a strong youth population.Recently, the Congress Working Committee decided that “CKG” will be held in 800 cities and towns – which means one in every district. Sources said Rahul may personally attend around 20 of them, while the rest will become a vehicle for the party to woo the youth.
Article Summary: The next episode of “chhatron ki goonj’ will be held in Indore on Sep 12. Congress has picked the venue owing to the fact that there has been a history of paper leaks in the state including the infamous examination scandal “Vyapam scam”

Uttarakhand CM's intervention ensures medical aid for ailing child. (Photo: ANI)

UTTARAKHAND: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has intervened to secure urgent medical aid for an eight-year-old boy suffering from a lifelong debilitating health condition.This comes after the Chief Minister visited a local food stall in Lohiahead, where the boy's father shared their struggle.Following CM Dhami's directions, Udham Singh Nagar District Magistrate Nitin Singh Bhadauria, along with Chief Medical Officer Dr SK Goswami, a team of doctors, Chief Development Officer Divesh Shasani and Sub-Divisional Magistrate Tushar Saini, visited Ravi Sharma's residence, whose eight-year-old son has been suffering from a health condition since childhood and is unable to move his hands and leg, according to a release from the CMO.CM Dhami visited Ravi Sharma's shop in Lohiahead on Sunday to have tikki. During the interaction, Ravi Sharma told the Chief Minister about his son Dev and his condition. The child has been undergoing treatment since birth, including treatment at Indresh Hospital in Dehradun.Orthopaedic specialist Dr HS Airi and the Chief Medical Officer examined the child and reviewed his previous medical history and treatment records.After the examination and assessment of his past treatment history, the doctors suggested that an MRI scan be conducted first, following which further treatment would be decided. The District Magistrate immediately directed officials to arrange the child's MRI scan the very next day.He said that the administration would provide a vehicle and necessary assistance to take the child and his parents to the district hospital. He assured the family that every possible effort would be made to ensure the child receives proper treatment and that no stone would be left unturned in his care.Earlier, on August 28, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami also announced the development of modern, high-tech toilets across the state, keeping in mind the convenience, safety and dignity of women."These facilities will be equipped with modern amenities and will give special attention to cleanliness, privacy, security and the essential needs of women."The Chief Minister said that the dignity and respect of women are among the state government's highest priorities.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has intervened to secure urgent medical aid for an eight-year-old boy suffering from a lifelong debilitating health condition. This comes after the Chief Minister visited a local food stall in Lohiahead, where the boy's father shared their struggle.

Article Title: PM Modi meets Iran president who seeks India's help to end war
Article Text:
File Photo: PM Modi holds a bilateral meeting with the President of Iran, Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the SCO Summit, in Bishkek

PM Narendra Modi called for freedom of navigation and commerce while stressing that civilians and civilian infrastructure, including commercial shipping and seafarers, must not be harmed under any circumstances in a meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek. Despite the threat of US sanctions, both leaders backed efforts to expand trade ties.The leaders discussed the West Asia situation, including the Strait of Hormuz situation and Chabahar port cooperation amid the threat of US sanctions, in what was their first formal bilateral meeting in nearly 2 years. Modi expressed concern over escalation of tensions and reiterated the significance of resolving all issues through dialogue and diplomacy, while seeking lasting peace and stability in the region.Blaming the US for failing to fulfil its commitments and declaring that continuation of war is not in the interest of humanity, Pezeshkian urged Modi to use India's "extensive" contacts to wean away parties involved from the path of bloodshed and war. The president also called for expanding bilateral cooperation in political, economic, scientific, cultural and other areas of mutual interest, saying this would neutralise the impact of sanctions and further elevate the relationship.Modi and Pezeshkian last had a bilateral meeting on the margins of the BRICS summit in Kazan in 2024. It provided an opportunity for both leaders to reaffirm their commitment to expanding economic cooperation, as Modi underlined India’s commitment to strengthening its long-standing “friendship” with Iran across diverse sectors.“We want to expand and diversify our trade basket in the times to come. We had a discussion on the prevailing situation in the region. India will continue to support all efforts aimed at ensuring lasting peace," said Modi in a post on X.According to an Iranian readout, Pezeshkian told Modi that despite efforts by the US and Israel to create roadblocks in Iran's ties with other countries, Tehran was ready to expand its cooperation with India across various fields.The readout also said that Modi backed Pezeshkian's view regarding the existence of groups that see their interests in the continuation of war. “I agree with you that there are those who see their interests in war, but we must intensify our efforts to establish peace. My belief and conviction is that, ultimately, peace and security will prevail," said Modi, according to Iran.Modi also reiterated India's readiness to closely cooperate with Iran in multilateral organizations, including BRICS and SCO and told Pezeshkian he was looking forward to welcoming him for the BRICS Summit in India.“From what I have come to know of your personality, you are a peace-loving person, and I believe that you can play an effective role in advancing the cause of peace. I am confident that your efforts will ultimately lead to positive results,” said Modi in the meeting, according to the Iranian readout.The PM was also quoted as saying that Iran and India have ancient and deep-rooted relations and this historical and cultural heritage can serve as a valuable foundation for expanding cooperation. Transportation and maritime affairs, developments related to the Strait of Hormuz, and progress in Chabahar port cooperation were among the most important issues discussed by the two sides, said the Iranian statement.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi called for freedom of navigation and commerce while stressing that civilians and civilian infrastructure, including commercial shipping and seafarers, must not be harmed under any circumstances. The leaders discussed the West Asia situation, including the Strait of Hormuz situation and Chabahar port cooperation. Despite the threat of US sanctions, both leaders backed efforts to expand trade ties.

NEW DELHI: Granting relief to Dehradun-based gym owner ‘Mohd’ Deepak Kumar against whom an FIR was lodged for confronting Bajrang Dal members, Supreme Court on Monday stayed the proceedings against him and sought a response from Uttarakhand govt on quashing of the case.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta also stayed operation of the order passed by Uttarakhand HC that had restrained Deepak from making social media posts about the incident and the case. Appearing for Deepak, senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi said his client had protected a Muslim shopkeeper and intervened after Bajrang Dal members objected to the shopkeeper using the word 'Baba' in his shop’s name.He said Deepak had gone to assist the shopkeeper after the incident and he had himself lodged complaints regarding the incident, but that no action was taken on them and instead an FIR was registered against him.“How can a good samaritan be subjected to this kind of a complaint?” Singhvi asked.The bench, after a brief hearing, agreed to examine the plea and granted interim protection to Deepak. “Issue notice. In the meantime, proceedings from the impugned FIR, effect and operation of the HC order to remain stayed,” court said.The case against Deepak pertains to offences under BNS sections 115(2) (causing hurt), 191(1) (rioting), 351(2) (criminal intimidation), and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace).
Article Summary: Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta also stayed operation of the order passed by Uttarakhand HC that had restrained Deepak from making social media posts. Appearing for Deepak, senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi said his client had protected a Muslim shopkeeper and intervened after Bajrang Dal members objected.

Article Title: Bihar, Jharkhand settle 25-year Sone water row
Article Text:
Bihar and Jharkhand signed a Sone river water-sharing agreement, resolving a long-standing dispute and ensuring water for irrigation and drinking needs.

NEW DELHI: Bihar and Jharkhand Monday signed a water-sharing agreement for Sone river, resolving a 25-year-old dispute over sharing of water between the two states.The agreement, signed here in the presence of union home minister Amit Shah and CMs of Bihar and Jharkhand — Samrat Choudhary and Hemant Soren respectively — will provide irrigation water to millions of farmers across vast rural areas of the states, while also ensuring access to drinking water for the people in both the states.Shah said the agreement is an excellent example of the ‘Team Bharat’ vision and cooperative federalism championed by PM Modi. “While all states possess their own distinct identities, if they move forward as ‘Team Bharat’ within the national context, there is no problem which cannot be resolved,” he said after the signing of the agreement.He said that issues concerning vast geographical areas, farmers, rural regions, and drinking water supplies in both states have been “permanently resolved” with the agreement.Sharing details, the home minister said the agreement would ensure the availability of adequate water for drinking and irrigation to a large population across the districts of Bhojpur, Buxar, Rohtas, Kaimur, Aurangabad, Arwal, Gaya, and Patna in Bihar. “Moreover, water would become available for irrigation and drinking purposes in Palamu, Garhwa, and other regions of Jharkhand,” he said.Though an agreement was reached among Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and undivided Bihar on the water sharing of Sone river and the cost of Bansagar dam in Madhya Pradesh in 1973, a dispute started in 2000 when Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar as a new state and it demanded a bigger share of water in Bansagar project as a large chunk of the catchment area came under it. Bihar, on the other hand, cited the 1973 agreement to claim water from the project.
Article Summary: Bihar and Jharkhand Monday signed a water-sharing agreement for Sone river, resolving a 25-year-old dispute. The agreement will provide irrigation water to millions of farmers across vast rural areas of the states. It will also ensure access to drinking water for the people in both states.

Article Title: 'Move from endless war to end of war': PM Modi tells Putin; key details from Bishkek talks
Article Text:

'Move from endless war to end of war'

PM Modi invites Putin for Brics Summit

PM Modi and Putin take car ride

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday met Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, where the two leaders discussed bilateral ties and key global developments."Had extensive discussions with President Putin. Discussed the full range of the India-Russia Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. It is gladdening to see significant progress across various sectors in recent years. Focus areas for the India-Russia friendship remain energy, innovation, space, fertilisers and people-to-people linkages," PM Modi said in a post on X.Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for an end to prolonged conflicts, saying that every day spent in war pushes humanity backwards, while steps towards peace bring renewed hope."Every day spent in war sets humanity back, whereas every step taken towards peace fills humanity with new hope and enthusiasm. We must move away from endless war and an end to the war. This is essential for the well-being of humanity," PM Modi said during his bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek.Referring to the Ukraine conflict, PM Modi said India had consistently discussed the issue with Putin and remained committed to supporting peace efforts."We have consistently discussed the issue of Ukraine. When we met previously, you briefed me in detail on all aspects of the matter. As you know, India supports all efforts towards peace and will continue to do so," he said.Calling for an early peaceful settlement, PM Modi said, "A peaceful resolution to all issues at the earliest is the call of humanity, and this is India's message. The land of Gandhi and the land of Buddha share a single message- the path of peace. Today, I look forward to discussing these matters with you," he added.PM Modi invited Putin to New Delhi for the upcoming Brics Summit in September."We are eager to welcome you to India for the Brics Summit in New Delhi this September," PM Modi said, adding that Putin's visit would "further strengthen India-Russia relations."Putin is scheduled to travel to New Delhi later this year for the summit.Putin thanked PM Modi for his role in maintaining India-Russia relations. "I'm very grateful to you for your personal attention to the Russia-India relationship," the Russian president said.The two leaders reviewed cooperation across areas of the bilateral partnership and exchanged views on pressing international issues.Following their bilateral meeting, PM Modi and Putin travelled together in the same car to the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games at Bishkek Arena.The meeting comes months after the last India-Russia Annual Summit, held in New Delhi during Putin's state visit on December 4-5, 2025. During that summit, the two countries adopted a joint statement and announced 21 outcomes, including 16 MoUs and agreements covering areas such as mobility, fertilisers, health, food safety, maritime cooperation, customs, commerce, academics and media.India and Russia have held 23 annual summits so far, alternately in the two countries. Their relationship was elevated to a "Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership" in 2010.Earlier, PM Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with the two leaders discussing the ongoing conflict in West Asia. It was their first bilateral meeting since the Iran-US conflict broke out in February."Calling for safeguarding the freedom of navigation and commerce, he (PM Modi) emphasised that civilians and civilian infrastructure, including commercial shipping and seafarers must not be harmed under any circumstances," MEA said.During the meeting, PM Modi reiterated India's support for efforts to end the conflict and stressed the importance of freedom of navigation and protecting civilians and civil infrastructure in the region. "Met President Masoud Pezeshkian in Bishkek. Reiterated our commitment to strengthening India’s long standing friendship with Iran across diverse sectors," PM Modi said on social media."We want to expand and diversify our trade basket in the times to come. We had a discussion on the prevailing situation in the region. India will continue to support all efforts aimed at ensuring lasting peace," he said.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. The two leaders discussed bilateral ties and key global developments. PM Modi invited Putin to New Delhi for the upcoming Brics Summit in September.

NEW DELHI: Women Commission chairperson Lata Gupta on Monday condemned the gangrape of a 16-year-old girl inside a moving sleeper bus and said those responsible must be punished. “The person behind this must get punishment. Immediate action was taken with the arrest of the bus driver and conductor,” Gupta said while speaking to news agency ANI.Police has subsequently arrested Kuldeep and Sandeep from a bus parking area in Timarpur and seized the sleeper bus."When a woman is facing any problem, if there is a lack of coordination among the agencies dealing with her case, it is the commission's responsibility to improve that coordination, whether with the courts or the police administration," she told news agency PTI.The Class 11 student from Uttar Pradesh was gangraped inside the bus after she boarded it seeking help while stranded in heavy rain, police said. The incident took place on the night of August 4 in Delhi, after the teenager, from Mainpuri district, left home following a disagreement with her family and set out to meet her cousin in Noida.According to police, the girl mistakenly got off at Pari Chowk amid heavy rain and darkness.An empty sleeper bus passing through the area stopped after she signalled for help. The driver, Kuldeep, and conductor, Sandeep, allegedly told her that the bus was headed towards Noida Sector 63 and allowed her to board.The bus then travelled nearly 47 kilometres towards Kashmere Gate. The accused allegedly abandoned the teenager on Ring Road near the Kashmere Gate bus terminal late at night and fled.The girl told police that both the driver and conductor raped her and threatened to kill her when she resisted.Monu Gupta, manager of the bus travel company that owns the vehicle, said the driver and conductor had been asked to take the bus to Timarpur for repairs. “We had asked the driver and conductor to take the bus to Timarpur for repair. The next morning, we received a call from the Administration; we were told that the bus had been seized and the driver and conductor were arrested,” he said.Gupta said both the driver and conductor were from rural Kanpur and had been working with the company for the past two years. “We have submitted their Aadhaar cards to the Police. They have been working here for the last two years,” he added.The driver and conductor have been arrested in connection with the case, and the bus has been seized as police continue their investigation.
Article Summary: DWC chairperson Lata Gupta condemned the gangrape of a 16-year-old girl inside a moving sleeper bus. Gupta said the person behind this must get punishment. The driver and conductor have been arrested in connection with the case, and the bus has been seized.

JAMMU: Six people died and three others, including an 11-year-old boy, were injured after the vehicle they were travelling in skidded off the road and plunged into a deep gorge in Surankote in J&K’s Poonch district on Wednesday.The accident occurred around 5.30pm. Officials suspected the driver had lost control of the vehicle, which rolled into the gorge, killing six occupants — Mohd Shafiq (32), Nazakat Hussain (34), Sheraz Ahmed (30), Musarat Naz (19), Mohd Fareed (21), and Zulfat Bi (25) — on the spot, police said.Upon receiving information, cops reached the spot and launched a rescue operation with the help of locals. Poonch chief medical officer Dr Parvaiz Ahmed Khan pressed ambulances into service to facilitate evacuation. The injured were initially admitted to a local health facility, from where two were shifted to GMC Jammu due to their critical condition, Dr Khan said.All victims and injured were residents of Seri Chouhana, police said, adding that the bodies were shifted to Poonch district hospital.J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha condoled the tragedy in an X post, stating that he had directed the district administration to provide immediate assistance to the affected families. JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. Article Title: SC judge complains against Rajasthan acting CJ; CJI Surya Kant seeks response

NEW DELHI: Responding to letters written by SC judge Sandeep Mehta complaining against Rajasthan high court acting chief justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and seeking his transfer outside the state, CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response.Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.Justice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC.CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” he said. He also released a public statement Wednesday decrying the attempt to hold a public trial over allegations made by one judge against another.Contents of the letters cannot be adjudicated in public domain and that judge concerned must be given a fair opportunity to place his response before any conclusion is reached.The fact that allegations have been made, therefore, cannot by itself be treated as a finding against the judge,” CJI Surya Kant’s statement said.The established mechanism for inquiring into allegations of an Supreme Court or High Court judge is the constitution of an in-house committee — comprising judges — by the Chief Justice of India, if he finds the response of the judge accused of misdemeanour or corrupt practices unsatisfactory and feels the charges are serious enough to warrant a deeper probe.CJI Kant, who is on a three-day official visit to Germany, also told TOI that he has already sought a response from Justice Sharma following the letters from Justice Mehta, who has alleged that there is “clear evidence of favouritism” by Justice Sharma. Justice Mehta’s complaints are being examined, CJI Surya Kant said.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response. Article Title: 'Country Babur came from': Owaisi takes dig at PM Modi's Uzbek honour

Owaisi pointed to Uzbekistan's historical connection with Babur

NEW DELHI: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi took a dig at the BJP after Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred Uzbekistan's highest state honour.PM Modi was presented with the Order of "Oliy Darajali Dustlik" by Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev during his two-day state visit to the Central Asian country. The honour is Uzbekistan's highest state award.Reacting to the recognition, Owaisi pointed to Uzbekistan's historical connection with Babur, who he said was born in the Fergana Valley in present-day Uzbekistan and founded the Mughal Empire in India."I congratulate the BJP; the very country from which Babur came to India has conferred an award upon the Prime Minister. The Fergana Valley is in Uzbekistan. Wherever the Prime Minister goes these days, he returns with an award. Congratulations. You used to hurl so many insults in Babur's name, yet the people of that very country are now honoring you with an award. The Sangh needs to reflect on this... We hope that members of the Sangh Parivar and RSS supporters will no longer speak of Babur in that manner," he said.The remarks come against the backdrop of the BJP and RSS's frequent criticism of the Mughal period and references to Babur in political discourse, particularly in discussions around the construction of the Ram temple in Ayodhya and India's history.PM Modi, meanwhile, thanked Mirziyoyev for the honour and described him as his "brother". He said India and Uzbekistan would work together for the welfare of the Global South and humanity."My friend, the father of the economic revolution in Uzbekistan, who has served as a role model across this entire region in scaling new heights of development--this two-day visit of mine will always be remembered," PM Modi said.Owaisi's comments on the award came while he was also criticising RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over his recent remarks on Hindu-Muslim unity. Bhagwat, speaking at the 'One World One Humanity' event in New York, said there was no difference between human beings and that different religious paths led to the same goal.Owaisi described Bhagwat's remarks as an "old trick from the RSS playbook"."What the current RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat has said is an old trick from the RSS playbook. They will never disavow or retract the things the RSS has consistently stated," he said."There is a distinct difference between the speeches they deliver for the outside world and those meant for their own members--this has always been their playbook style," Owaisi said.

Article Title: 100-year-old Hindu temple demolished in Pakistan’s Punjab
Article Text:
PMMP chairman Aslam Parvez Sahotra said he met Punjab Additional Home Secretary on August 28 and submitted a written application seeking action against those allegedly responsible for the demolition, as well as officials accused of failing to protect the property.

A more than 100-year-old Hindu temple in Pakistan ’s Punjab province was demolished on August 21 in Siraj village of Narowal, around 130 km from Lahore, with minority groups alleging that religious zealots targeted the site to absorb its land into an adjacent madrassa. The government, however, has maintained that the temple collapsed because of torrential rains.The demolition has triggered demands for an investigation and restoration of the temple, with the Pakistan Masiha Millat Party (PMMP) accusing local authorities and the Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB) of failing to protect the centuries-old Hindu place of worship.PMMP chairman Aslam Parvez Sahotra said he met Punjab Additional Home Secretary on August 28 and submitted a written application seeking action against those allegedly responsible for the demolition, as well as officials accused of failing to protect the property.Sahotra alleged that the people involved in the demolition were associated with the Tehreek-i-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP), a banned far-right Islamic party. He further claimed that after the temple was brought down, metal fittings from its shikhar, bricks and other material were removed from the site.The temple, estimated to be between 100 and 125 years old, stood on approximately 1,000 square metres of land in Siraj village.The dispute over the site predates its demolition. According to Sahotra, land adjoining the temple had earlier been leased by the ETPB for a madrassa. The lease was subsequently cancelled after rent allegedly went unpaid for several years and the premises were not used for the stated purpose.He said several people later occupied portions of the property illegally.Sahotra referred to a revenue department report which identified individuals as illegal occupants of the temple’s quarters and other parts of the property. He said the ETPB deputy administrator in Sialkot cancelled the seminary’s lease rights on January 29, 2026, and ordered the eviction of illegal occupants and sealing of the property.“This order was not implemented,” Sahotra alleged.A report attributed to the DSP Narowal, dated April 11, also indicated that local police were aware of security concerns surrounding the temple and the possibility that it could be damaged, according to Sahotra.The ETPB, however, has rejected the allegation that the temple was deliberately demolished.ETPB senior official Rana Iftikhar told PTI that the temple had collapsed following torrential rains. He acknowledged its historical significance, saying, “The temple carries no name in our record books. However, it is a very old one... more than 100 to 125 years old,” he said.Iftikhar also confirmed that the land adjoining the temple had been leased for a seminary, but maintained that the temple's own land had not been leased.“However, the temple's land is not given to anyone for lease,” he said and added the ETPB highups will decide about restoration of the temple.The conflicting accounts have heightened concerns among members of the local Hindu community.Hindu community leader Rattan Lal condemned the demolition and called for the government to order the temple's restoration. He said the district administration and ETPB had failed to take adequate steps to secure the site or remove alleged illegal occupants.“The district administration and the ETPB failed to take adequate measures to protect the site or remove the alleged occupants, ultimately allowing the temple to be demolished,” Lal said and asked the government to take action against those found involved in the demolition of the temple.Lal, who is also a Hindu member of the Narowal District Peace Committee and the Pak Dharam Astan Hindu Committee, said members of the community were now reluctant to approach the site.“We are even afraid to visit the site because of the madrassa that continues to operate on its premises.”Sahotra has called for the temple to be rebuilt in its original form and urged the Punjab government to strengthen protection for Hindu temples, Sikh gurdwaras and Christian churches, along with their adjoining properties.Arya, meanwhile, said decades of conflict between Pakistan and India, the Islamisation policies of the 1980s and the 1992 demolition of the Babri Masjid in India had contributed to a sense of insecurity among local Hindus.“Preserving Hindu heritage can improve the image of Pakistan and attract tourism.”
Article Summary: More than 100-year-old Hindu temple in Pakistan's Punjab province was demolished on August 21. Minority groups claim the temple was demolished to make way for an Islamic madrassa. The Pakistan Masiha Millat Party (PMMP) has submitted a written application seeking action against those allegedly responsible.

Article Title: Indian among 12 killed after Russia launches massive strike on Ukraine
Article Text:
The Kyiv and Odesa regions were the main targets of the assault

At least 12 people, including an Indian, were killed after Russia launched a massive aerial assault across Ukraine overnight, Ukrainian authorities said on Tuesday. More than a dozen people were also wounded, including three children.The attack, which began at around 6pm on Monday, involved ballistic, cruise and anti-radar missiles, along with 218 drones and decoys, according to Ukraine’s air force. Around a third of the drones were reportedly jet-powered.The Kyiv and Odesa regions were the main targets of the assault, which marked the sixth consecutive day of Russian attacks on the Ukrainian capital.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said residential buildings and civilian infrastructure were damaged in several areas. “Overall, 12 people were killed, among them an Indian citizen, and dozens more were injured in the attack.”Zelenskyy said seven people were killed in a strike on a railway depot in Kyiv, while authorities reported another death in the city’s Holosiivskyi district after a non-residential building was hit and caught fire. A drone also struck a residential building in the Solomianskyi district, where emergency workers rescued a man and freed a woman trapped under rubble.In the wider Kyiv region, three people were killed and 12 wounded. In Boryspil, several buildings and vehicles were damaged, while emergency crews evacuated 48 people and rescued two people from beneath the rubble.Odesa also came under heavy attack, with residential buildings and civilian infrastructure damaged. A sewing factory caught fire, while Russian forces also struck the Orlivka international ferry crossing on the border with Romania.Ukraine’s air force said its forces destroyed or suppressed 199 aerial targets, including five ballistic missiles and 187 drones. Missile and drone strikes were recorded at 28 locations, while debris from intercepted targets fell at another 10 sites.Zelenskyy said the attacks showed the need for stronger air defences, adding: “Russia always plans its strikes specifically to cause as much destruction to people’s lives as possible, and it succeeds only when air defense capabilities are insufficient.”
Article Summary: The Kyiv and Odesa regions were the main targets of the assault. It marked the sixth consecutive day of Russian attacks on the Ukrainian capital. The attack involved ballistic, cruise and anti-radar missiles. Around a third of the drones were reportedly jet-powered.

Article Title: Nepal flash floods death toll crosses 1,000; thousands still missing
Article Text:
Indian pilgrims survive after being diverted from flood-hit route

Families seek missing relatives as Nepal begins identification process

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority for the governments of Nepal and China post-flood? Providing immediate relief to affected families Long-term rehabilitation plans Enhancing emergency preparedness 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The death toll from the catastrophic floods that devastated Nepal and China has crossed 1,000, with authorities reporting 987 deaths in Nepal and 16 in China. Rescue teams continue efforts to reach communities cut off by destroyed roads, bridges and landslides.Nepal’s disaster agency said on Tuesday that 3,916 people remain missing, including 583 foreigners. At least 11,814 people have been rescued so far, with emergency crews using helicopters and other aircraft to reach stranded communities in areas where the floodwaters and landslides have severed road links.The disaster struck on August 26 after a chain of events high in the Himalayas. A glacial collapse sent huge volumes of rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods that swept through parts of Tibet and Nepal.Scientists studying satellite imagery said the collapse appears to have been caused by the failure of bedrock beneath a glacier. The rockfall was powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.The resulting torrent of water and debris rapidly swelled rivers flowing through the Himalayan valleys, sweeping away homes, buildings, roads and bridges and carrying mud and rocks downstream. Meanwhile, Nepal has issued a fresh flood alert as water levels rise across several districts, adding to concerns over further disruption as rescue and relief operations continue.Among those safely evacuated were 39 Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims from Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu, who returned to India after being diverted from their original route because of the floods.The pilgrims had crossed into China before the disaster and escaped the worst of the flooding. Their return journey was rerouted with assistance from Chinese, Nepalese, Tamil Nadu and Indian authorities."There were 39 people in our group; we started the journey from our village. Our route was to Kerung; from that route, we reached Mansarovar. While returning, the accident took place. Everything was taken away by the flood, immigration was affected, and none of the villages was left," one pilgrim, Yogesh, told ANI.The ministry of external affairs has said 158 Indian citizens have so far been safely evacuated from Nepal.With thousands still missing, the Indian Embassy in Nepal has issued procedures for families trying to identify the mortal remains of Indian citizens killed in the floods. Relatives can use photographs and descriptions published by Nepal Police, while DNA matching with first-degree relatives will be required where remains have been temporarily interred or cannot be identified visually.Nepal has temporarily interred a large number of remains to prevent health risks, making forensic identification particularly important as rescue and recovery operations continue.
Article Summary: Nepal's disaster agency said on Tuesday that 3,916 people remain missing, including 583 foreigners. At least 11,814 people have been rescued so far, with emergency crews using helicopters and other aircraft to reach stranded communities. Rescue teams continue efforts to reach communities cut off by destroyed roads, bridges and landslides.

Article Title: ‘For a more inclusive campus’: In a first, a visually impaired student in Dusu race
Article Text:
Pankaj Dhingra, a 1st-year LLB student at Campus Law Centre and a Kirori Mal College graduate, has been associated with AAP for three years.

TOI





NEW DELHI: A visually impaired student could make history in the Delhi University Students’ Union (Dusu) elections, with Pankaj Dhingra likely to enter the fray for the central panel as a candidate of AAP’s student outfit, ASAP. If his candidature is finalised, he would be the first such student to formally contest a central panel election in Dusu.Dhingra, a first-year LLB student at Campus Law Centre and a Kirori Mal College (KMC) graduate, has been associated with AAP for three years. He was the secretary of the students’ union at KMC and has been active in raising issues concerning persons with disabilities (PwD). He toldhe has around 5-10% vision and described his condition as “late blindness”, with his vision beginning to deteriorate when he was in classes V-VI.The lack of representation of PwD students in DU’s student bodies was a major reason motivating him to contest, Dhingra said. Lack of tactile infrastructure, commuting difficulties and problems faced by visually impaired students in finding examination scribes are among key issues he wants to raise.“Students are appointed as scribes but aren’t paid remuneration for a long time. Because of this, visually impaired students face difficulty in finding people to write their exams.It’s also tough to find suitable subject-matter experts as scribes,” he said.Dhingra participated in the CJP-led stir at Jantar Mantar under the ASAP banner and alleged he was lathicharged. He also expressed solidarity with students following the death of an IIT Delhi student.The probable ASAP panel includes former NSUI state secretary Janhvi Kataria; AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar’s nephew Abhishek Kumar; Kunal Tyagi, son of MCD councillor Pinky Tyagi; and Ashmit Panwar.Tyagi, a second-year LLB student and graduate of Motilal Nehru College, joined ASAP last year after it was relaunched. His father, Naresh Tyagi, is a district president. Kumar, a BA graduate of Shyam Lal College who is seeking admission to an MA in Buddhist Studies, was appointed state vice-president when the student outfit was relaunched. He is being projected as the Dalit representative.Kataria, an ARSD College graduate and a Najafgarh resident, joined ASAP four months ago after spending around four years with NSUI. The lone woman among the probables, she is being projected as a representative of students from outlying areas who face long daily commutes to DU. Panwar, a first-year PGDAV College student, is a recent entrant to ASAP.ASAP state vice-president Kamal Tiwari said the decision to field a visually impaired student was a “conscious step” towards meaningful representation for students with disabilities, adding the aim was to create a more “inclusive and representative campus”.The final list will be clear once the nomination and withdrawal process is completed after Sept 11.Meanwhile, RSS-affiliated ABVP announced a list of 13 probables -- Alok Attri, Ayushi Sharma, Ishu Maurya, Krishna Yadav, Lakshya Raj Singh, Nitin Tanwar, Priyanshu Mahamana, Riya Chhawri, Riya Malik, Sunny Dedha, Tanya Mavi, Varun Yadav and Yash Dabas. It said they will visit 47 colleges and five departments of DU to interact with students and incorporate their inputs in the manifesto.The Dusu elections will be held Sept 18 and results will be announced Sept 19.
Article Summary: Pankaj Dhingra likely to enter the fray for the central panel as a candidate of AAP’s student outfit, ASAP. If his candidature is finalised, he would be the first such student to formally contest a central panel election in Dusu. He has around 5-10% vision and described his condition as ‘late blindness’

Article Title: 6 devotees killed, 14 injured after pickup truck rams into parked truck on KMP expressway in Haryana
Article Text:
The collision took place when the devotees were travelling towards Vrindavan





PALWAL: Six devotees, including three women, were killed and 14 others seriously injured after a Tata pickup carrying a group of pilgrims rammed into a truck parked along the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal (KMP) Expressway in Palwal district in the early hours of Tuesday.The collision took place when the devotees were travelling towards Vrindavan after visiting religious sites in Rajasthan. The impact was so severe that both vehicles were badly damaged, leaving the passengers trapped and injured.The group, comprising around 21 people from Mainpuri district of Uttar Pradesh, had left their villages on Friday to visit religious sites. On Monday evening, they visited the Khatu Shyam temple and Salasar Balaji temple in Rajasthan before starting their journey towards Vrindavan in Mathura.According to police, the pickup reached the KMP Expressway in Palwal district early Tuesday when it crashed into the truck that was parked on the roadside.The collision triggered panic among the passengers, with cries for help heard from the mangled vehicle. Passersby reached the spot and began rescue efforts before informing the police and emergency services.The injured were taken to the District Civil Hospital in Palwal, where doctors declared six people dead.The deceased have been identified as Vijay Singh, Raj Kumar, Reshma Devi, Kamla Devi, Sudha and Mahesh.The 14 others were injured and are undergoing treatment at Palwal Civil Hospital.Police have taken the bodies into custody and sent them for postmortem examination.Cops are waiting for the families of the deceased to reach the hospital and complete the identification and other formalities before conducting the autopsies.
Article Summary: The group, comprising around 21 people from Mainpuri district of Uttar Pradesh, had left their villages on Friday to visit religious sites. They visited the Khatu Shyam temple and Salasar Balaji temple in Rajasthan before starting their journey towards Vrindavan in Mathura.

Article Title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke dares Maharashtra govt to file cases against him, says must fix schools
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said, Expired food items are being used to feed children in govt schools





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday challenged govt to file “not one but 100 cases” against him if exposing poor conditions in zilla parishad schools was a crime, insisting that FIRs would not stop his School Theek Karo (fix the schools) campaign.During visits to zilla parishad schools at Lohgaon and Karanjala in Hingoli taluka, Dipke inspected classrooms, benches, drinking water facilities and material used for preparing mid-day meals.Villagers and social activist Munir Pathan accompanied him and highlighted problems faced by students and staff.Dipke said he has been touring govt schools across Maharashtra to draw attention to inadequate infrastructure and other shortcomings.“Is it a crime to visit schools and point out the problems and lack of facilities there? If it is, file not one but 100 cases against me, but please ensure that the schools are improved,” he said.In a video shared on social media, Dipke alleged that expired spices were being used in mid-day meals served to students.“Expired food items are being used to feed children in govt schools. Would those sitting in power feed the same food to their own children? And if exposing this means FIRs against us, then please go ahead.We won’t stop exposing the truth,” he said.Dipke alleged that many govt schools lacked basic facilities, with insufficient benches and poorly maintained toilets.He also criticised the disparity between public and private education. “It is unfortunate that children of govt officials and elected representatives study in air-conditioned private schools while children from ordinary families are forced to study in classrooms in poor condition,” he said.Referring to ongoing tribal student protests, Dipke urged govt to address their concerns without delay.“Students are the future of the country. Govt should not ignore their issues any further,” he said.Dipke demanded that rural zilla parishad schools be provided infrastructure and amenities comparable to those available in private schools in cities such as Mumbai and Pune.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday challenged govt to file ‘not one but 100 cases’ against him if exposing poor conditions in zilla parishad schools was a crime. Dipke said he has been touring govt schools across Maharashtra to draw attention to inadequate infrastructure and other shortcomings.

Article Title: ‘Tortured in class, led to depression’: Mother after 12-year-old Delhi girl’s death
Article Text:
The Delhi government has ordered an inquiry into the girl’s death.





NEW DELHI: A 12-year-old Delhi schoolgirl died days after her mother alleged that she was “tortured” and left distressed following an incident with a teacher at her government school in East Vinod Nagar on July 22.“My daughter was tortured in class, leading to her depression. No one from the school came to see her when she was unwell,” the girl’s mother alleged.The Class VII student died on August 27. Her family alleged on Monday that the teacher had scolded and beaten her on July 22, following which she fell ill and her condition deteriorated.The Delhi government has ordered an inquiry into the girl’s death.Education minister Ashish Sood said the teacher has been transferred with immediate effect to ensure that the investigation is conducted fairly and without interference.Police said the girl had a history of epilepsy. They added that no complaint was made against the teacher between the alleged incident and the girl’s death.The family also cremated her on the day she died and approached Kalyanpuri police station with the allegations only on Monday.According to the family, the girl was allegedly scolded by the teacher on July 22 for not carrying a book and was asked to stand at the back of the classroom.She was reportedly unwell at the time. The school then called her family, who took her home before she was later taken to hospital.Police are examining the allegations, the sequence of events following the incident, the girl’s medical records and her course of treatment.Sood said the government was treating the matter with “utmost seriousness and sensitivity” and assured that strict action would be taken if the inquiry established any negligence, dereliction of duty or irregularity.According to a Delhi government official, the education director also met the principal of the school in connection with the matter.
Article Summary: A 12-year-old Delhi schoolgirl died days after her mother alleged that she was “tortured” and left distressed following an incident with a teacher. Her family alleged on Monday that the teacher had scolded and beaten her on July 22. The Delhi government has ordered an inquiry into the girl’s death.

Article Title: CCTV, mobile data, Manipur trail: How police cracked Chennai's torso-in-suitcase murder
Article Text:
caught on camera: Footage from Chennai Central station showed the couple with the bag





CHENNAI: A day after an Assam man and his wife were brought to Guduvanchery in connection with the murder and dismemberment of a 38-year-old woman, police said the victim was killed after she refused to terminate her pregnancy and pressured the man to marry her.Hayathun Nisha, 38, a native of Odisha, was murdered at a rented house on Mosque Street, Guduvanchery, earlier this month. Her dismembered remains were subsequently transported in a suitcase aboard Tamil Nadu Express.Guduvanchery police, using CCTV footage, mobile phone data and other technical evidence, traced Manik Uddin Laskar, 22, of Assam, and his wife Bhagabati Majhi, of Odisha, at Kashimpur in Jiribam district of Manipur on Saturday. The couple was arrested and brought to Guduvanchery on Sunday for further investigation.The murder came to light on Aug 5, when the Tamil Nadu Express, which had departed Chennai Central for New Delhi on Aug 3, reached Agra Cantonment railway station. Railway police checked an unclaimed suitcase in a general compartment found the dismembered remains of a woman inside.As the train had originated in Chennai, investigators began examining CCTV footage from Chennai Central and other railway stations along the route.Footage showed a man and a woman carrying the suitcase, and police subsequently traced their movements to Guduvanchery.The investigation eventually led police to the rented house on Mosque Street, where Nisha had been staying. Police said additional body parts were recovered from a large cooking vessel in the house. Investigators began probing her relationship with Manik Uddin, and found that Nisha had become pregnant and had been pressing him to marry her.She had refused to terminate the pregnancy, leading to frequent disputes. Police suspect Manik Uddin and his wife then decided to kill Nisha. After the murder, her body was dismembered and some of the remains were packed into the suitcase, which was taken to Chennai Central and placed aboard the Tamil Nadu Express, investigators said.During interrogation, the couple told police that Nisha’s head was shaved after it was severed. They initially tried to fit the head into the suitcase but, when they were unable to do so, smashed it into smaller pieces before packing the remains inside, police said. Police suspect this was done to make identification difficult.Police are also coordinating with Agra railway police to trace the victim’s missing remains and establish whether all the body parts transported on the train have been recovered.
Article Summary: Hayathun Nisha, 38, a native of Odisha, was murdered at a rented house on Mosque Street, Guduvanchery, earlier this month. Her dismembered remains were subsequently transported in a suitcase aboard Tamil Nadu Express. Police traced Manik Uddin Laskar, 22, of Assam, and his wife Bhagabati Majhi, of Odhya, at Kashimpur in Jiribam district of Manipur on Saturday.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu farmer ends life after losing Rs 15L in FQL scam
Article Text:
A farmer from Kasampatti, Raj.





MADURAI/DINDIGUL: A farmer from Kasampatti near Natham allegedly died by suicide after losing Rs15 lakh in the suspected FQL investment scam, triggering a road blockade by his relatives on the Natham-Madurai National Highway.Amid growing outrage, DGP Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal on Monday transferred all six related cases to the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) for a detailed inquiry.According to police, the deceased Raj had allegedly invested Rs15 lakh believing claims that it will double. On realising that he had fallen victim to an investment fraud, he was devastated, and subsequently hanged himself in a tree near Kasampatti, police said. A senior police official told TOI that 21 accused have been arrested so far from Madurai, Sivaganga, Dindigul and Virudhunagar districts in connection with the multi-district fraud through an app called FQL linked to cryptocurrency.Raj’s relatives blocked the road near Vathipatti junction carrying his body, demanding action against those responsible for the scam. Though police held talks with the protesters, they refused to withdraw causing severe traffic congestion on the busy stretch. Additional police personnel were deployed to regulate traffic. A case was registered by Natham Police, and further investigation is underway.The official said several bank accounts linked to the suspects have been frozen.Authorities have also initiated steps to freeze cryptocurrency wallets used by the accused. A non-transaction request has been issued to the registration authorities to prevent the sale, transfer, or alteration of immovable properties linked to the accused. Lookout circulars (LOCs) have also been issued against key suspects, the official added.Meanwhile, revenue officials set up a special camp at Madurai district collectorate campus, where 193 petitions related to the scam were received. Altogether, around 37,000 complaints connected to the FQL scam have been received in Madurai district so far.
Article Summary: Raj’s relatives blocked the road near Vathipatti junction carrying his body, demanding action against those responsible for the scam. 21 accused have been arrested so far from Madurai, Sivaganga, Dindigul and Virudhunagar districts. Authorities have also initiated steps to freeze cryptocurrency wallets used by the accused.

Article Title: Stalked from garage for weeks, entered while she slept: Chilling details emerge in Hyderabad nurse's rape-murder
Article Text:
Police arrested a bike mechanic from Bihar for the alleged rape and murder of a nurse.





HYDERABAD: Police on Monday arrested a bike mechanic from Bihar for the alleged rape and murder of a nurse in Pahadishareef, saying he had been watching her movements for nearly a month before allegedly entering her room through a window while she slept.According to police, the accused, who came to Hyderabad in 2023 for work, was employed at a garage located close to the rear window of the room where the nurse lived. Investigators said he first noticed the woman through the window about a month before the crime and allegedly began monitoring her movements thereafter.Police said the accused entered the room through the window while the nurse was asleep and allegedly attempted to sexually assault her. She resisted, following which he allegedly strangled her to death before escaping through the same window.However, investigators said they could not conclusively establish whether the sexual assault occurred before or after the woman's death. The accused allegedly told police that she was unconscious when the assault took place.“Whether the victim had died by then or not cannot be ascertained,” an investigating officer said.Police said the accused was allegedly under the influence of alcohol when he committed the crime. After the incident, he reportedly returned to the garage and went to sleep. He initially denied involvement in the murder.Investigators subsequently analysed mobile phone tower data and other evidence and questioned him again, following which he allegedly confessed to the crime. Police also recovered hair strands and other forensic evidence from the scene.Investigators said the victim's belongings, including her mobile phone and headphones, were left untouched, suggesting that robbery was not the motive.The crime came to light when the woman's friend, unable to contact her, went to her room with a few others. Finding the door locked, they entered through the window and found her dead.The case was initially registered as a murder. Following the medical examination, police added sections relating to rape as well as provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.The accused will be produced before a magistrate. Police are also checking with Bihar authorities to determine whether he has any previous criminal record.The victim had moved to Hyderabad from Kothagudem about seven months ago and was working as a nurse at a private hospital. She was staying in accommodation close to her workplace.
Article Summary: Police arrested a bike mechanic from Bihar for the alleged rape and murder of a nurse in Pahadishareef. He allegedly entered her room through a window while she slept and strangled her to death. Investigators said they could not conclusively establish whether the sexual assault occurred before or after the woman's death.

Article Title: Bus fresh from repairs, no passengers aboard: How UP teen was lured, gang-raped and dumped in Delhi

NEW DELHI: A family row, a wrong stop, and an empty bus returning from a repair workshop set off a chain of events that ended in the alleged gang-rape of a 16-year-old girl from Uttar Pradesh, police said on Monday.Stranded amid heavy rain and darkness after getting off at the wrong stop, the teenager was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving sleeper bus after boarding the vehicle seeking help, police said. The bus then travelled nearly 47km before the teenager was allegedly abandoned near Kashmere Gate.The incident took place on the night of August 4 after the teenager, from Mainpuri district, left home following a disagreement with her family and set out to meet her cousin in Noida.According to police, the girl got off at Pari Chowk by mistake amid heavy rain and darkness. An empty sleeper bus passing through the area stopped after she signalled for help.The driver, Kuldeep, and conductor, Sandeep, allegedly told her that the bus was headed towards Noida Sector 63 and allowed her to board.Police said the conductor allegedly began making obscene advances towards the teenager soon after the bus started moving.The girl, in her complaint, alleged that both the driver and conductor subsequently raped her and threatened to kill her when she resisted.The sleeper bus had curtains around its berths, which police said allegedly helped the accused conceal what was happening inside during the journey.The bus travelled nearly 47km towards Kashmere Gate. The accused allegedly abandoned the teenager on Ring Road near the Kashmere Gate bus terminal late at night and fled.The terrified student approached Kashmere Gate police and reported the incident.Police subsequently arrested Kuldeep and Sandeep from a bus parking area in Timarpur and seized the sleeper bus. The vehicle has been sent for forensic examination.Police said the bus had earlier broken down and was taken to a workshop in Surajpur for repairs. After the repairs were completed, the driver and conductor were taking the empty bus to Timarpur when they encountered the teenager at Pari Chowk.Monu Gupta, manager of the bus travel company, said the bus had been parked at Himgiri, Surajpur, from July 27 to August 4 for repair work due to a sensor-related issue."We had asked the driver and conductor to take the bus to Timarpur for repair. The next morning, we received a call from the administration, we were told that the bus had been seized and the driver and conductor were arrested," Gupta said.Recounting the bus's movements, Gupta said the vehicle was taken out of Himgiri around 5pm on August 4 after the repairs were completed. The driver and conductor later moved it out again around 9pm and were instructed to proceed towards Timarpur."We had parked the car in Himgiri to repair it. When it was repaired on the 4th of August, we took the car from there. We took the car out of Himgiri at 5 in the evening." "After that, they parked the car a little further from there. They took the car out at 9. After taking the car out at 9, we told them to go to Timarpur."Gupta said the company expected the bus to reach Timarpur but instead received a call from Delhi authorities the following morning informing them that the vehicle had been seized. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A 16-year-old girl from Uttar Pradesh was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving sleeper bus. The bus had broken down and was taken to a workshop in Surajpur for repairs. After the repairs were completed, the driver and conductor were taking the empty bus to Timarpur. They encountered the teenager at Pari Chowk amid heavy rain and darkness.

Article Title: As Google renames 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' in the US; company's 'update' on what users in the US, Canada and 'rest of the world' will see
Article Text:
Google statement on the name chang

Canada PM Mark Carney on US renaming the Lake Ontario

Trump sends direct message to Apple to change the name

Escalating the trade dispute with Canada, US President Donald Trump last week announced that he was changing the name of the smallest of the five Great Lakes. As the trade talks between the US and Canada broke down, leading to a wave of tariffs and retaliatory tariffs, Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America'.After Trump's announcement, Google began rolling out this change for US users. The company posted a brief update on its Google Maps blog, noting that it follows the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for its maps. This primarily means that the company has to rename Lake Ontario in Google Maps. Google's update on the name change also made it clear that the change will be only for Google Map users in the US. According to Google, those in the US will only see the new name, which is 'Lake of America'. Meanwhile, Canadians will continue to see the 'Lake Ontario' label. In the rest of the world, Lake Ontario will take precedence, but Lake America will also be there in parentheses."The U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) has formally changed the name for "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States. Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the U.S.,people using Maps in the U.S. will see "Lake America," those in Canada will continue to see "Lake Ontario," and those outside of the U.S. and Canada will see both names. These updates follow our long-standing policy for bodies of water with names that vary from country to country, and are starting to roll out now," said the company in a blog update.In a post on X, formerly Twitter, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney wrote, "The name Lake Ontario comes from the Wendat word Ontari’io, which, appropriately, means “the lake is beautiful, the lake is big”. The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America. We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms. Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario – then, now and always."President Trump has reportedly "reached out to Apple directly" about changing Lake Ontario's name to Lake America in Apple Maps. According to US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, “The president reached out to Apple directly, so I’m sure that we may be seeing that change coming up soon to Lake America.” Burgum shared the same in an ‌interview ⁠on Fox Business’ “Mornings with Maria” programme.
Article Summary: The U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) has formally changed the name for "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States. According to Google, those in the US will only see the new name, which is 'Lake of America' Meanwhile, Canadians will continue to see 'Lake Ontario'

Article Title: Zohran Mamdani goes to court to stop a law passed by New York City Council to give $10,000 bonuses to teachers that he supported during election campaign
Article Text:
Zohran Mamdani

What the bonuses passed by the New York City Council would cover

Zohran Mamdani’s legal argument

Why the council moved forward anyway

The Mayor's office responds

A Zohran Mamdani caught between principle and precedent

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has filed a lawsuit to stop a law passed by the New York City Council granting one-time $10,000 bonuses to low-paid school aides, known as paraprofessionals. The move marks a surprising break with the United Federation of Teachers (UFT), which endorsed Mamdani in last year’s mayoral election and had his support for the bonuses during the campaign. According to a report by the Wall Street Journal, the City Council unanimously passed the legislation in late July, covering around 25,000 school aides whose salaries start at $32,000. Mamdani allowed the bill to become a law without veto but sued days later, arguing the bonuses would cost the city $325 million and violate collective bargaining rules. His lawsuit asserts that compensation must be determined through negotiations between unions and the mayor, not legislation, warning that the council’s move sets a precedent for bypassing bargaining.The bonuses passed by New York City Council covered roughly 25,000 city school aides who are also known as paraprofessionals, who typically work with students with special needs and whose salaries start at around $32,000.In July this year, the City Council unanimously agreed also passed a legislation granting these workers one-time $10,000 payments. At that time, Mamdani also chose not to veto the bill, allowing it to automatically become law. However, later Mamdani sue the council in state court, arguing the bonuses would cost the city an estimated $325 million.In pursuing the lawsuit, Mamdani is asserting his executive authority over labor-contract negotiations. The suit argues that the bonuses violate a decades-old law requiring that compensation be determined through collective bargaining between unions and the mayor's office, not through City Council legislation. According to the lawsuit, allowing the bonus law to stand would set a troubling precedent, opening a path for unions to secure pay increases that bypass the traditional give-and-take of contract negotiations entirely.City Council Speaker Julie Menin, a Democrat, said the council had hoped Mamdani would negotiate pay raises for paraprofessionals directly or include salary increases in this year's budget. When neither happened, the council proceeded with its own legislation. Menin argued the aides are underpaid, and that raising their salaries would help fill the roughly 1,600 current vacancies in the role while lowering education costs over the long run. She framed the raise as both ethically and fiscally sound.UFT President Michael Mulgrew, whose union represents 200,000 members, said in a statement that the council's legislation was necessary to address chronic workforce shortages and was designed in a way that legally protects the collective bargaining process. Mulgrew had earlier warned, in a New York Times interview this summer, that he would wage an "all-out war" if Mamdani tried to block the legislation. His union filed a motion this week to formally intervene in the court case.A mayoral spokesman said the administration filed the lawsuit to keep negotiations between the city and its workforce centered at the bargaining table rather than being decided through political intervention. The spokesman added that Mamdani's office has been in active talks with the teachers union to address fair compensation for school aides.As per the WSJ report, Evan Stone, chief executive of the teacher-led advocacy group Educators for Excellence, described the council's legislation as putting Mamdani in a genuinely difficult position. According to Stone, Mamdani agrees in principle that school aides deserve higher pay, but feels he needs to defend the traditional process for setting citywide compensation — historically, mayors have relied on pattern bargaining to apply a standard percentage raise across city union contracts, avoiding a situation where one group receives a disproportionately large increase relative to others.Stone said allowing this particular bonus to stand could call the entire historical bargaining process into question at a moment when the city is already facing tight budget constraints. He also acknowledged the political risk to Mamdani, noting that some teachers who supported his campaign may feel frustrated that he hasn't followed through on a promise he backed as a candidate.Michael Petrilli, president of the education reform think tank Thomas B. Fordham Institute, said this kind of rift between a Democratic politician and teachers unions is notable, since conventional political wisdom generally holds that Democratic officials try to avoid conflict with such an important part of their political base.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has filed a lawsuit to stop a law granting one-time $10,000 bonuses to low-paid school aides. The City Council unanimously passed the legislation in late July, covering around 25,000 school aides whose salaries start at $32,000. The move marks a surprising break with the United Federation of Teachers (UFT), which endorsed the mayor in last year's election.

Article Title: 'We're going your way': How NCR teen's plea for help after tiff with parents ended in gang-rape on moving bus, dumped 30km away
Article Text:
A 17-year-old girl seeking help after leaving home was gang-raped on a moving sleeper bus.





NEW DELHI: A 17-year-old girl’s search for help after leaving home following a tiff with her parents allegedly ended in a nightmare inside a moving sleeper bus, where two men offered to take her “your way” before allegedly gang-raping her and abandoning her around 30km away near Kashmere Gate.The teenager had left her home in Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh, and planned to travel to Noida Sector 63 to meet her cousin and uncle. On the night of Aug 4, she reached Greater Noida's Pari Chowk but reportedly got off at the wrong spot amid heavy rain and darkness.Stranded and searching for help, she signalled an empty sleeper bus passing through the area.The driver and conductor stopped and allegedly told her that they were headed towards Noida Sector 63, allowing her to board the vehicle.What the girl did not know, police said, was that the bus was not operating on any passenger route at the time.The two accused — driver Kuldeep and conductor Sandeep, both from Kanpur — had allegedly been instructed to take the vehicle for repairs. The bus had been at a workshop in Surajpur since July 27 because of a malfunctioning sensor and was taken out on Aug 4 for further repairs in Timarpur, according to the travel company's manager.As soon as the bus began moving, the conductor allegedly started making advances towards the teenager.Police said the two men sexually assaulted her inside the moving sleeper bus as it travelled from Pari Chowk towards Noida Sector 63, with the driver and conductor allegedly taking turns at the wheel.“The accused stopped and told her the bus was headed towards Noida Sector 63 and allowed her to get in,” a senior police officer said.DCP (North) Niharika Bhatt said both men sexually assaulted the girl inside the moving bus and threatened to kill her when she resisted.The assault allegedly took place over a stretch of around 30km between Pari Chowk and Noida Sector 63. Curtains covering the bus windows meant that nothing inside the vehicle was visible from the road.After reaching the Noida side, the bus continued towards Delhi.The accused allegedly abandoned the teenager on Ring Road near Kashmere Gate, apparently believing that taking her far away from the alleged crime scene would make it harder to link them to the offence.The girl then approached police and reported the incident.Delhi Police took cognisance of the case after the complaint was filed in the capital, even though the alleged assault took place in Noida. Investigators traced the accused to Timarpur, where both were found resting inside the bus and arrested within hours of the complaint.The UP-registered sleeper bus has been seized and sent for forensic examination, while police have also collected CCTV footage from along the route taken by the vehicle. The chargesheet in the case is likely to be filed this week, police said.The teenager was later produced before the Child Welfare Committee and handed over to her father in compliance with its directions.The case has also raised fresh questions over private buses operating across Delhi-NCR and the safety of passengers, particularly women travelling alone.The bus involved in the case was registered in Firozabad in April and had an all-India permit, according to Noida assistant regional transport officer Udit Narayan Pandey. However, it was being operated by a Noida-based travel company.Private buses and shuttles have increasingly filled gaps in public transport across NCR, often picking up passengers from informal stops in Greater Noida, Noida and Delhi. While registration, valid permits and licences are mandatory, police verification of drivers and conductors is also required — a provision that officials have acknowledged is not always effectively enforced.The Delhi Commission for Women has taken suo motu cognisance of the incident and directed that the investigation be expedited, seeking an action-taken report within seven days.
