After they abandoned the teenager on Ring Road near Kashmere Gate and fled, she approached the police station there and reported the incident.Investigators traced the accused to Timarpur and arrested both of them. The UP-registered sleeper bus has been seized and sent for forensic examination. Cops have seized CCTV footage along the route taken by the bus.The teenager was produced before the Child Welfare Committee and, in compliance with their orders, handed over to her father.Ravi Shankar Nim, DCP Greater Noida said Delhi Police had not provided any information regarding the incident to the Noida Police prior to Aug 31. "There are certain discrepancies between the authentic evidence available in connection with the incident and the version that has been issued. It is also noted that the survivor's side has not provided any information regarding the incident to Gautam Buddh Nagar Police either," Nim said.Sources in UP police said they had contacted the transporter who said there were passengers in the bus till Mayur Vihar and denied any assault as reported by the minor. Delhi Police, however, said the bus was not plying on a route and that no passenger was present at the time of the incident.Delhi Commission for Women has taken suo motu cognisance of the matter and ordered that the probe be expedited and an action-taken report be submitted within seven days.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped in a moving sleeper bus she boarded in Greater Noida's Pari Chowk on Aug 4. The accused - the driver and conductor - were nabbed within three hours of the crime. Delhi Police took cognisance after the girl filed a complaint in Delhi, and initiated a probe.

Article Title: Heavy rain triggers flood scare across UP, Uttarakhand; Ganga, Yamuna water levels rise
Article Text:
The torrential rains across northern India have led to flood-like conditions along several major river basins, affecting multiple districts in Uttarakhand and UP

(With agency inputs)





DEHRADUN: Heavy overnight rainfall in Dehradun and adjoining areas caused the Tamasa River, which flows through the premises of the historic Shri Tapkeshwar Mahadev Temple, to swell significantly, local officials said on Tuesday.The torrential rains across northern India have led to flood-like conditions along several major river basins, affecting multiple districts in Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh.In Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj, rising water levels in both the Ganga and Yamuna rivers forced floodwaters into residential settlements along the riverbanks, causing distress among residents and prompting municipal authorities to keep response teams on alert.Similarly, in Varanasi, the water level of the Ganga River has been continuously rising due to sustained heavy rainfall upstream, inundating low-lying areas and disrupting routine activity along the city's prominent ghats.Local administrations across the affected regions are closely monitoring the situation, with emergency service personnel deployed near riverbanks to prevent any untoward incidents.Meanwhile, all government, private, and non-government schools from Classes 1 to 12 as well as Anganwadi centres in Dehradun district will remain closed on Tuesday in view of the forecast for heavy to very heavy rainfall, lightning, and extremely heavy spells of rain in parts of the district, officials told news agency ANI.The one-day holiday was declared by Dehradun District Magistrate and District Disaster Management Authority chairperson as a precautionary measure following the issuance of an Orange alert.According to the order issued on August 31, the latest weather forecast and nowcast indicated the possibility of severe weather conditions over the next 24 hours.The Chief Education Officer and District Programme Officer, Dehradun, have been directed to ensure strict compliance with the order across all educational institutions.Meanwhile, the water level of the Ganga in Rishikesh has risen amid continuous heavy rainfall in the hilly areas of the Garhwal division, though the river remains below the warning mark, officials said.The Ganga was flowing swiftly at Triveni Ghat. However, officials from the Central Water Commission said the river level was still within the normal range and below the danger threshold.Amid rising water levels, teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Water Police and Disaster Relief Teams have been deployed at major ghats across Rishikesh, Muni Ki Reti and Lakshman Jhula.Emergency personnel are also making regular announcements over loudspeakers, urging devotees, tourists and local residents to exercise caution and stay away from the riverbanks.
Article Summary: Torrential rains across northern India have led to flood-like conditions along several major river basins, affecting multiple districts in Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh. The Tamasa River, which flows through the premises of the historic Shri Tapkeshwar Mahadev Temple, has swollen significantly.

Article Title: BMC gets transfer, promotion recommendations for 225 officials, employees
Article Text:
Mumbai:





BMC received recommendation letters for the transfer or promotion of as many as 225 officials and employees over the past year. The recommendations were made by Union ministers, state cabinet ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs and corporators cutting across party lines, as mentioned against respective names on the list. This information was obtained by activist Anil Galgali from the office of BMC city engineer in reply to a query filed under the Right to Information (RTI) Act.According to Galgali, a preliminary analysis of the political names mentioned against the 225 officials and employees showed that the names of certain political leaders appear repeatedly.Deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde ’s name appears 10 times, followed by Union minister of state Ramdas Athawale , whose name appears nine times. The names of state ministers Girish Mahajan and Kalidas Kolambkar appear seven times each.Similarly, the names of Shiv Sena MLA Mangesh Kudalkar, Deputy Speaker in Legislative Assembly Anna Bansode and Shiv Sena MLA Tukaram Kate appear six times each. The names of BJP MLA Murji Patel and Shiv Sena MLA Dilip Lande appear five times each.The names of NCP minister Narahari Zirwal, BJP MLA Sumit Wankhede, Shiv Sena leader Rahul Shewale, Shiv Sena MLA Prakash Surve, NCP minister of state Indranil Naik, Shiv Sena MLA Santosh Bangar, BJP MLAs Ram Kadam and Kishan Kathore, and MLC Bachchu Kadu appear four times each.Further, the names of BJP minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, NCP minister Hasan Mushrif, Shiv Sena ministers Bharatseth Gogawale and Uday Samant, BJP MLA Parinay Fuke, Shiv Sena MP Ravindra Waikar,BJP MLCs Prasad Lad and Pravin Darekar, and Shiv Sena (UBT) MLAs Sunil Prabhu and Mahesh Sawant appear three times each.The names of Shiv Sena Union minister of state Prataprao Jadhav, BJP state ministers Pankaja Munde, Mangal Prabhat Lodha and Jaykumar Gore, MP Raosaheb Danve, Shiv Sena Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi, Assembly Speaker Rahul Narwekar and NCP MLA Sana Malik appear two times each. The names of BJP state president Ravindra Chavan, BJP state minister Chandrakant Patil and NCP state minister Sanjay Bansode appear once each.Galgali said, “Transfers in the municipal corporation are expected to be carried out on the basis of administrative requirements, seniority and transparent criteria. However, a list containing the names of ministers, MLAs, MPs and public representatives against the names of 225 officers and employees has now come to light. The list includes officers and employees holding the posts of assistant engineer (AE), sub engineer (SE), executive engineer (EE) and junior engineer (JE). ”Galgali further stated that disciplinary action is expected to be taken in accordance with the existing rules. “Therefore, a thorough investigation should be conducted immediately. If any unauthorised interference, pressure or irregular process is found in the transfer process, appropriate action should be taken against the concerned officers and employees as per the provisions of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888. ”Ganesh Khankar, BJP leader of the House in BMC, said most of these recommendations were made on humanitarian grounds.“I have personally recommended the transfer of an official whose father was ailing and he wanted a posting near his residence. In another instance, one lady official sought a transfer to a post closer to her home, as she was a single mother and had to take care of her young children. In both cases, how could anybody refuse their request? Besides, there is pressure on the local public representatives for recommendations from local citizens and party workers. Most have genuine problems; therefore, they are seeking recommendations for transfer.”According to Shiv Sena BMC Group Leader Amey Ghole, recommendations have been given by representatives of all parties across the spectrum and are not restricted to one party alone.“These officials and employees have various problems. Some have health issues and some cannot travel for long distances, so they seek recommendation for a transfer. These engineers approach their local MLA, sometimes in their native place. Besides, party workers too come with requests.”
Article Summary: BMC received recommendation letters for the transfer or promotion of as many as 225 officials and employees over the past year. The recommendations were made by Union ministers, state cabinet ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs and corporators cutting across party lines, as mentioned against respective names on the list.

Article Title: Leak detected from tanker carrying benzene in Mumbai’s Chembur area, no one hurt
Article Text: Mumbai: A leak was detected from a tanker carrying approximately 35,000 litres of benzene near Mysore Colony Monorail station in Chembur on Monday night, causing panic in the area. No one was injured in the incident which took place around 8pm, said officials.Senior station officer K V Shirke and station officer Sagar Khopde led the fire brigade team that swung into action and created a 500m buffer zone as decanting of benzene from the affected tanker into an empty tanker was completed successfully. Traffic was stopped on Mysore Colony Road and Mahul Road and operations at Mysore Colony Monorail station were halted during this period."The driver of the tanker, which had left from BPCL refinery premises, informed the authorities about the leak from the flange of the draining system, which is attached to the tanker body," said a fire brigade official. "Initially, we carried out water fogging on both sides of the tanker to ensure that no vapour cloud was formed due to the benzene leak. We wanted to ensure that no spark travelled and no ignition was caused as benzene is highly flammable and combustible."A HAZMAT vehicle was pressed into service and we decanted benzene from the leaking first compartment of the tanker, which has five compartments, to another tanker. After decanting, we moved both the tankers to the saffe control section of the BPCL refinery," said the fire brigade official.Rupesh Madhavi, a Shiv Sena (UBT) activist, said that chemical tankers are usually double parked illegally on roads in the vicinity of residential areas. A little away from the spot there is a school, where international level gymnasts practice. "We had warned residents that they may have to shift in case of an eventuality. However, the situation was brought under control," he said. " Around 2,000 chemical tankers are parked on the roads in the area. Local corporator Snehal Shivkar has been demanding that a truck terminus be developed by the BMC for parking chemical tankers."In another incident, a tanker carrying glacial acetic acid tilted after getting stuck in a roadside chamber on LBS Marg in Mulund West. No leakage was detected. The incident was reported near Vaishali Nagar at 8.52pm. A fire brigade team and ward office officials reached the spot and efforts were underway to pull out the tanker with the help of a crane.
Article Summary: A leak was detected from a tanker carrying approximately 35,000 litres of benzene near Mysore Colony Monorail station in Chembur on Monday night. No one was injured in the incident which took place around 8pm, said officials. The driver of the tanker, which had left from BPCL refinery premises, informed the authorities about the leak.

Article Title: Two youths arrested for teen auto driver's murder after argument over exorbitant fare
Article Text: Navi Mumbai: Two days after an 18-year-old auto rickshaw driver was found murdered on the pavement along the mini seashore road in sector 10A, Vashi, the Vashi police in coordination with the crime branch unit-1 and central unit teams conducting a parallel probe arrested two accused youths by tracing them to Mankhurd on Monday.On Saturday around 4 am, a woman on a morning walk had informed the Vashi police about a boy lying unconscious and bleeding on the pavement. The police reached the spot and found the teenager had sustained multiple injuries on his head, neck and hands due to assault using some sharp weapon. He was declared brought dead at NMMC hospital, Vashi and was identified as Sujan Kumar Feku Mahato, a resident of Ghansoli.ACP (crime) Bhausaheb Dhole informed that the arrested accused are Sahil Ananda Surve (20) and Sahil Yashwant Kharat (20), both residents of Maharashtra Nagar area, Mankhurd. The accused Surve is a history-sheeter as a criminal case was registered against him at Trombay police station in 2024 for the offences of murder attempt and causing grievous injuries and under the Indian Arms Act. He was arrested by Trombay police and was released on bail on Oct 7, 2025.ACP Dhole said, “After contacting the victim Mahato’s family, it was learnt that he worked at a roadside Chinese food stall in Koparkhairane and daily whole night, he drove his father’s auto rickshaw to ferry passengers for supporting his family financially.His mother informed that as per daily routine, on Friday around 9 pm, he had left home with his father’s auto rickshaw to ferry passengers. As the auto rickshaw being driven by Mahato was missing from the crime scene, it was suspected that the assailant might have stolen his auto rickshaw after dumping his body on the pavement. Accordingly, the CCTV camera footages were scanned in Ghansoli and Koparkhairane areas when the auto rickshaw was spotted near Koparkhairane railway station from where two passengers had boarded Mahato’s auto rickshaw.”ACP Dhole added, “The CCTV footages of the route from Koparkhairane till Vashi were scanned and the auto rickshaw was spotted crossing Vashi toll plaza. Accordingly, the auto rickshaw was traced till Mankhurd and the two suspect youths were detained as the stolen auto rickshaw was recovered from them. During interrogation, the duo Surve and Kharat confessed to their crime by giving statement to the police that on Saturday around 3.40 am, they boarded Mahato’s auto rickshaw near Koparkhairane railway station to reach Mankhurd, but Mahato demanded exorbitant fare of Rs 150. They told him they had only Rs 100 and could pay that much, but Mahato was reluctant to ferry them. Hence, they threatened him at knife point and forced him to ferry them till Mankhurd for ₹100. On the way, when the auto rickshaw reached Vashi mini seashore road, Mahato received a mobile call. Mahato told the duo youths in his vehicle to get down as he had received a call from another local passenger. Hence, an argument ensued between them and Surve attacked Mahato with a knife causing grievous injuries on his head, neck and hands. As Mahato fell unconscious, the duo dumped him on the pavement near a garden on the mini seashore road and escaped in his auto rickshaw.
Article Summary: 18-year-old auto rickshaw driver was found murdered on the pavement along the mini seashore road in sector 10A, Vashi. Sahil Ananda Surve (20) and Sahil Yashwant Kharat (20), both residents of Maharashtra Nagar area, Mankhurd, were arrested on Monday.
